{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb",
      "line": 11,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Migration crashes when embed_category has no matching setting row",
      "body": "The migration runs `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the `embed_category` lookup. That setting was optional and `site_settings` only stores rows that were changed, so when it is absent (or blank, so the join matches no category) `execute` returns no rows, `[0]` is nil, and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The fallback lookup for `uncategorized_category_id` makes the same nil assumption. Use `first`/`find_by` and guard before dereferencing."
    },
    {
      "file": "db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Migration copies old host values raw and interpolates them into SQL",
      "body": "The old `embeddable_hosts` SiteSetting accepted schemes and paths (the removed code parsed them with URI and old specs used `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`). The migration puts `h` verbatim into the new column via `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing `EmbeddableHost` normalization and also not escaping quotes. Records like `http://eviltrout.com` or `example.com/1234` can never match `record_for_host`'s `URI(referer).host` comparison, so existing embeddings stop working after upgrade; a quote in the old setting also breaks the migration. Normalize and parameterize the insert."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/embeddable_host.rb",
      "line": 17,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Host matching drops the port while validation allows it",
      "body": "Validation explicitly allows an optional `:port`, and `before_validation` keeps it (it only strips the scheme and path). But `record_for_host` matches `URI(referer).host`, which omits the port, against the full stored `host`. A saved host such as `example.com:3000` therefore never matches a referer whose host is `example.com`. Either reject ports in validation or compare `host:port` consistently. The bound lookup value is also not downcased, so a mixed-case referer host can miss a lower-cased row."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/embeddable_host.rb",
      "line": 2,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than five characters",
      "body": "The regex requires the TLD to be `[a-z]{2,5}`, so valid hostnames such as `example.museum`, `example.travel`, or modern long TLDs cannot be saved as embeddable hosts. Admins cannot configure otherwise valid embedding sources. Use a looser hostname check or rely on URI parsing."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/embeddable_host.rb",
      "line": 2,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "No uniqueness constraint on host makes the category mapping ambiguous",
      "body": "Neither the model nor the migration enforces a unique host (case-insensitively). The admin UI can create two rows for the same host with different categories, and the migration can copy duplicates from the old newline list. `record_for_host` then returns whichever row the database returns first, making the category used for new embedded topics non-deterministic. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and matching unique index."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb",
      "line": 10,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Missing ids cause 500 instead of a clean not-found response",
      "body": "`update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If the id does not exist, `save_host(nil)` calls `nil.host=` and `nil.destroy` raises. A stale admin UI request gets a 500 instead of a clean 404/JSON error. Use `find_by` and return an error when nil."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6",
      "line": 200,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Plural embedded ids are deleted even when hydration fails",
      "body": "In the new plural branch, `obj[k].map(...)` can return `undefined` entries when the side-loaded collection is absent or partial, but the code still assigns `obj[plural] = hydrated` and deletes the original `*_ids` key. Unlike the singular branch, it never checks whether lookup succeeded. That silently changes the model shape and loses ids for any rest_serializer payload that sends `foo_ids` without all `foo` objects (or without a `foos` collection). Preserve the original ids unless every reference resolves, and don't create arrays of undefined."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 43,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Feed imports can lose their configured category after this change",
      "body": "The category for every imported embed is now `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id)`. Feed polling imports arbitrary feed item URLs through `TopicEmbed.import` without going through `TopicRetriever`'s host check; if the feed host was not also in the old `embeddable_hosts` list, the migration creates no record for it and `category_id` becomes nil. Existing feed-polling installs will start creating uncategorized topics (or fail when uncategorized topics are disabled) instead of using the old `embed_category` setting. Migration/fallback needs to cover the feed-polling host."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6",
      "line": 38,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "UI clears the category after saving with the uncategorized fallback",
      "body": "When saving a host without a selected category, the server assigns `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the success handler overwrites `host.category` with `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, where `categoryId` is null. The table then shows a blank category until reload even though the host was saved to the uncategorized category. Use the category returned/assigned by the server, or map the null id to the uncategorized category."
    },
    {
      "file": "test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6",
      "line": 111,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Embedded test requests fruit 2 but only ever checks fruit 1",
      "body": "The test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the pretender's `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`), and the assertions still expect `[1,2]`. The test passes without exercising banana/id 2 (`color_ids: [3]`), so it does not verify id-specific embedded hydration. Update the fixture to return the requested fruit or keep the test on id 1."
    },
    {
      "file": "spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb",
      "line": 5,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Admin endpoint specs only assert inheritance",
      "body": "The new admin controller specs contain only a subclass assertion. None of the new create/update/destroy behavior is tested: host normalization, category assignment/fallback, missing ids, destroy, or authorization. These endpoints currently contain 500 paths, and the migration behavior is also untested. Add request specs for the happy path and missing-id/error cases."
    }
  ]
}
